courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course has a number of learning outcomes in which you will apply and demonstrate safe work practices and use tools and shop equipment. You will also use fasteners and fittings, lift and support loads, operate equipment, and service wire rope, bearings and seals. In this occupational skills course you will identify lubricants, and use welding equipment, electronic media and record keeping practices. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to successfully service and repair hydraulic brake systems, service and repair hydraulic power brakes, and service and repair air brakes. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to successfully describe hydraulic system principles, components and system types, and to service hydraulic components. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to successfully describe electricity, magnetism, and circuit components; interpret wiring diagrams and symbols, and use electrical testing instruments, service batteries, charging systems, starting systems, and electrical circuits. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to successfully service steering systems, service, diagnose, and repair suspension systems, remove and install undercarriage, and diagnose and repair frames. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to successfully service landing gear and trailer accessories, service and repair coupling systems, and service, diagnose, and repair trailer body components, heating systems, and refrigeration systems. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to successfully identify heating and air conditioning components, describe the construction and operation of heating and air conditioning systems, describe the impact of CFCs on the environment and apply legislated procedures when dealing with systems containing CFCs. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to repair advanced cab and body structures. In this course you will learn to describe truck and bus cab, bodies and components, and to service truck and bus cab, the bodies and their components. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to learn the design and operation of the charging, starting, electrical, and electronic systems, the components of the vehicle management system, and how to perform inspection, diagnosis and repair of these systems. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the skills required to describe the fundamentals of engines, diesel fuel injection, and alternative fuel systems. You will also learn to remove engines and components and to diagnose and repair engine support systems, diesel supply, engine emissions, alternate fuel systems, engine brakes, mechanical and electronic fuel systems. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to describe, diagnose and repair truck hydraulic assisted steering systems and to align a vehicle. In this course you will learn to describe geometry and types of alignment, diagnose alignment problems and perform an alignment. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will provide you with the fundamental skills required to describe and diagnose hydraulic systems, and the hydraulic system components. You will also learn to service and repair the hydraulic system, components, and electronic hydraulic systems. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will provide you with the skills required to diagnose and repair advanced brake systems. In this course you will review air brake systems and describe air brake schedules and their components. You will progress to diagnose and repair anti-lock braking systems. Here you will also learn to describe, diagnose and repair the air over hydraulic braking systems and their components. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will provide you with the basic skills for effective communication in a heavy duty truck shop, including a discussion of relevant working conditions and business practices. Written and oral skills to produce a job package will prepare you for successful employment, together with an explanation of the Truck Transport Mechanic (TTM) apprenticeship process. On-the-job communication among employees, management and customers will be practiced through presentations. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the administration skills, knowledge and practice necessary to contribute to the operation of an effective shop. You will also learn the skills to represent your employers effectively in a positive and professional manner to a customer, following established policies and procedures. Areas of study include staff responsibilities/roles within a service facility, service department, forms, procedures and information system utilization. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to service Carrier / Thermo-King Refrigeration Systems, diagnose, remove and repair refrigeration components and recharge systems. Onboard diagnostic processes are also covered. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to describe gear ratios and power transfer principles and methods, the operation, diagnosis and repair of clutches, manual, automated, automatic and power shift transmissions. In this course you will also learn the principles, operation, repair and diagnosis of the drivelines, drive axles, final drives, driveline retarders, along with power take-offs and transfer cases. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

T​his course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to describe then perform the basic tune-up and preventative maintenance procedures of the DD13/15 Detroit Diesel engines. This course includes an overview of after-treatment devices (ATD), electrical components and new emission components. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to learn how all the components of the fuel system, from the fuel tank to the injector, work together on a properly-running engine. Based on that knowledge you will learn to use the latest electronic service routines and to diagnose fault code or symptom-based issues with the fuel system. This course will cover the evolution of the DD engine fuel system from its initial EPA07 release through the latest GHG17 release. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001
​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to diagnose, service and repair Detroit Diesel after-treatment systems. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to describe alternating current (AC) generators. You will also learn to identify components and perform maintenance and diagnostic procedures on AC generators. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to describe Cummins engines, fuel systems and the EGR/ SCR after-treatment systems with VGT. This course will include the mechanical and electrical sub-systems, cooled EGR and exhaust after-treatment system. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to describe the Paccar MX engines. In this course you will also learn the Davie diagnostic software, exhaust turbochargers, engine braking assemblies, and fuel and exhaust after-treatment, lubrication, and cooling systems of the MX engines. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

courses.course_name: Communication Skills for the Heavy Duty Truck Industry
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to successfully communicate in writing and verbally within the heavy duty truck industry with managers, supervisors, government inspectors or with the public. You will complete record keeping through the use of appropriate forms, documents and media, following service manual procedures and manufacturer technical bulletins. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

​This course will introduce you to fundamental accounting principles and processes used by Service Managers to assess the performance of service operations. Referencing a business plan, you will explore fixed and variable operating costs including equipment purchase or renewal, insurance coverage, labour needs and building overhead. Pricing strategies for business sustainability and growth will be evaluated through the job costing approach. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

courses.prerequisite_raw: HDMT 1001 and completion of the BCIT HDTT term 1 and term 2 courses, and the co-op pre-employment workshops
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Cooperative Education (Co-op) involves enhancing the educational experience by integrating traditional academic studies with relevant work experience. You will work full time at the employer's work site for the duration of the Co-op work term period. The Co-op work term is a full time paid position where you will complete productive tasks that relate to the heavy duty truck industry. The Co-op position is approved by the Co-op Coordinator. Students in the program attend a pre-employment course to enhance their employability prior to their Co-op work term and compete for jobs posted during the first academic term. During the work term, students are monitored by BCIT. Prerequisite(s): HDMT 1001 and completion of the BCIT HDTT term 1 and term 2 courses, and the co-op pre-employment workshops

​This course will introduce you to the fundamentals of emerging and advanced technologies in the heavy duty truck industry. You will acquire fundamental skills in working with the latest technologies and alternate fuel / propulsion systems including: compressed natural gas (CNG), liquid propane gas (LPG), fuel cell technology, autonomous controls and guidance systems, electric vehicles and high voltage systems. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamentals of the fuel, combustion and emission chemistry as it applies to ignition and compression engines, and applied research as it relates to over-the-road transportation. You will participate in the Emissions Reduction and Research Test Hub (ERRTH) engine emissions testing using portable emissions measuring system (PEMS), dynamometers and advanced equipment. You will also engage with industry supplied projects such as electric vehicles, or participate in conversions of internal combustion engines to fully electric propulsion and energy storage systems. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course involves independent research of a practical or theoretical nature on a specific topic in heavy duty truck technology. You will seek approval before commencement of your proposed capstone project. Your capstone project is intended to provide a culminating experience that will allow you to demonstrate proficiency in several of the learning outcomes that are set forth by your diploma program. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will prepare you for the Authorized Inspector examination. This authorization permits inspection and decaling of various private and commercial vehicles in which the student was successfully graded on. Up-to-date information on recent changes to the inspection program will also be covered. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course is an introduction to vehicle software programming. You will learn the basic diagnostic vehicle sub-systems, vehicle inter-connecting networks and how to perform software programming and updates. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001
​This course will prepare you to write Red-Seal type questions typically found on ITA Standard Level Exams (SLE) and Certification of Qualification examinations. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

​This course will introduce you to the fundamental skills required to describe the fundamentals of AC motors and controls. Isolation and simple testing of these systems will be covered. Prerequisite(s): HDTT 1001

admission.raw: Scheduled intakes Domestic applicants: January each year International applicants: February and May each year *Scheduled intakes are subject to change. Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. When available intakes are full, qualified applicants are wait-listed. If you are uncertain or don’t meet the requirements, we strongly recommend you complete any applicable Trades Entry Assessments before applying. Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: one of the following: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent or BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment What if I don’t meet these English requirements? Math: one of the following: Pre-Calculus 11 (50%) or Foundations of Math 11 (50%) or Workplace Math 11 (50%) or Other acceptable BC and Yukon courses or BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment BCIT Mechanical Reasoning Trades Entry Assessment Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] Step 2: Department assessment Applications will be reviewed and assessed by the program area when the entrance requirements are complete. Qualified applicants will be contacted to attend an informational interview with the program area. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Recommended for success Minimum 12 months work or industry experience. Knowledge and background in the industry is an asset. A driver’s licence is strongly recommended in order to move vehicles in and out of the shops (a course completion requirement). Applicants are encouraged to attend an Heavy Duty Truck Technology Information Session for additional program details. High school graduation is recommended by SkilledTradesBC. Please refer to the SkilledTradesBC website for current apprenticeship prerequisite information. Applicants with medical or physical disabilities should contact Accessibility Services to arrange an interview. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program does not meet the eligible field of study requirement (CIP) and is therefore not eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. ( CIPC : 47.0613) Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Go back Overview Next up Advanced Placement
